title: Flea treatment
subtitle: From Mitch's answers 6 Nov 2026, plus official health department notes where he said to look it up. Items marked in orange are still to confirm.
source: Mitch's answers 6 Nov 2026; LPC Tech Onboarding Pack (PPE, never list, what you can quote, certificate note); jobbook-data/chemicals.json (Flea Treatment products); jobbook-data/services.json (past wordings); past inspection report wording in the treatment history; researched, not from Mitch: Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 19 (Fleas), Better Health Channel (Victoria) fleas page, Healthy WA fleas page

sections.heading: When this job comes up
body: Fleas in a home, including end of lease flea treatments. Mitch's service is called Flea Treatment. Past invoices read: "Flea Treatment", "End of lease flea treatment" and "Flea treatment end of lease internal & external".
Mitch doesn't always inspect first. If fleas are suspected he sometimes just treats. [Mitch to confirm: is a tech to do the same?]
End of lease: the client gets the certificate. The invoice usually does that job, unless they ask for something else.
Once you are experienced you can quote flea jobs. Anything complex goes to Mitch.
The job process, the never list, PPE and the free service period are in the Every job guide. [Mitch to confirm: does the free service period apply to this job?]

sections.heading: PPE
sections.title: PPE on before you go in
sections.note: Never apply chemicals without PPE. If the SDS requires it, you wear it. No exceptions.
items: Gloves and closed shoes at minimum
Gloves, mask and eye protection for any spray, as per the product SDS

items.text: Subfloor entry: coveralls, gloves, dust mask, torch
Roof void entry: dust mask, gloves, torch, appropriate footwear

sections.heading: Before you arrive
sections.title: What the customer can do before you get there. [Mitch to confirm: which of these do you actually ask for?]
items: Vacuum
Wash pet bedding
Lift items off the floor
Move pets out

sections.heading: Products Mitch uses
sections.title: Names as in Mitch's product list. No rates here: follow the label. [Mitch to confirm: which of the two bifenthrin sprays goes inside, and which product goes in the subfloor and outside]
rows: Country Bifenthrin 100 Low Odour Termiticide & Insecticide
Bifenthrin spray on skirtings, carpets and other surfaces inside
Bifenthrin spray on skirtings, carpets and other surfaces inside
Into cavities, walls and the roof

sections.heading: Where to treat
rows: Skirtings, carpets and other surfaces inside
Bifenthrin spray. [Mitch to confirm: bedding and under furniture too?]
Not really. Sometimes on bad cases. A past inspection report noted a heavy flea infestation in the subfloor and around the perimeter and said it should be treated.
One past invoice reads "internal & external". [Mitch to confirm: is that every end of lease job?]

sections.heading: Steps
sections.title: Steps
items: Ask the customer about their pets, where they sleep, when they last treated, and where the fleas are worst
Take BEFORE photos of the problem areas

items.text: Coopex into the cavities, walls and roof
items.detail: Dust only. Roof void entry PPE applies.

items.text: Bifenthrin spray on skirtings, carpets and other surfaces inside
items.detail: Country Bifenthrin or Aquastar from the products table.
Subfloor entry PPE applies. [Mitch to confirm: which product in the subfloor]

items.text: Apply per the product label. Never exceed label rates
items.detail: Never mix chemicals without checking the label first. If in doubt, call Mitch.

items: Keep chemicals away from food, children and pets
Note anything you could not treat or reach, and why
Take AFTER photos

items.text: Tell the customer not to vacuum or mop for a while
items.detail: They can go back in once it has dried. Follow the product label. [Mitch to confirm: how long is a while?]

items.text: End of lease: the client gets the certificate
items.detail: The invoice usually does it. [Mitch to confirm: what do you do if the agent or client wants something other than the invoice?]

sections.heading: How long until the fleas stop
body: Fleas can keep turning up for a while after the treatment. Adult fleas hatch out of their cocoons over about 5 to 14 days, and die when they touch the product on the surfaces. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 19 (Fleas), not from Mitch]

A second treatment may be needed. Government health advice is to repeat the spray 10 to 14 days later (Healthy WA), or once or twice more because flea eggs can survive for some weeks (Better Health Channel). [Mitch to confirm: from Healthy WA and the Better Health Channel, not from Mitch. When do you suggest a second treatment?]

sections.heading: Job complete when
items: BEFORE and AFTER photos taken
Areas booked have been treated, or noted with the reason they were not
Anything you could not treat or reach is noted on the job report, with the reason
Product, rate, area and quantity recorded on the job report
Customer told what you did, and not to vacuum or mop for a while
Customer told they can go back in once it has dried, as the product label says
End of lease: the client has the certificate (the invoice usually does it)
Service report left, or customer told it is being emailed

items.q: How long before we can go back in? And the pets?
items.a: Once it has dried. Follow the product label. [Mitch to confirm: pets the same as people?]
Not for a while after the treatment. [Mitch to confirm: how long is a while?]

That's normal for a bit. Fleas keep hatching out of their cocoons for the next 5 to 14 days, and they die when they touch the treated surfaces. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 19 (Fleas), not from Mitch]

items.q: Do I need to treat my pets too?
items.a: Yes, treat the pets as well or the fleas keep coming back. Ask your vet what to use. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 19 (Fleas) and the Better Health Channel, not from Mitch]

items.q: Will I need a second treatment?
items.a: Sometimes. If fleas are still around after a couple of weeks, tell us. [Mitch to confirm: from Healthy WA and the Better Health Channel, not from Mitch. What do you tell them?]

items.q: I need an end of lease certificate.
items.a: The client gets it. The invoice usually does the job, unless they ask for something else.

sections.heading: Tell Mitch straight away if
sections.body: Call Mitch on 0432 181 689. After hours or urgent, call Mitch directly.

items.detail: Stop immediately. Do not continue. Call Mitch.
Follow the SDS procedure. Call Mitch immediately. Never leave a spill unattended.
Treat the injury first. Call Mitch. Write down what happened.

items.text: The customer complains or gets aggressive
items.detail: Stay calm and do not argue. For a complaint, tell them Mitch will call them today. If they are aggressive, remove yourself. Call Mitch either way.

items.text: The customer asks for a quote on anything complex, or you are not sure
items.detail: Say "I'll need to get Mitch to come and have a look and provide a quote for that."

items.text: You see signs of termites or other pests outside this job
items.detail: Photograph it and tell Mitch. Termite quotes always go to Mitch.
